body.p: This is responsive to the Office Action mailed on September 24, 2024. With this response, claims 1, 8, and 10 are amended. This application continues with claims 1-13. Reconsideration and allowance of all of the claims is respectfully requested.
I. Claim Rejections - 35 USC Q 112

Claims 1-13 were rejected under 35 USC 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention. Applicant respectfully disagrees with this contention. However, the claims have been amended for clarification.
Claims 1 and 10 have been amended to clarify the movement "in a roll axis" and about a "pitch axis" as described throughout the specification at paragraphs [0042], [0045] for example.
Claim 8 has been amended to depend from claim 5 which introduces the first and second actuators.
At least in view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that the claims satisfy the
requirements of 35 USC 112(b). It is respectfully requested that this rejection be withdrawn and the claims allowed.
II. Claim Rejections 35 USC Q 102

Claims 1-4, 7 and 10 are rejected under 35 USC 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Smith et al. (US 4,283,152). Applicant respectfully disagrees with this contention. However, the claims have been amended for clarification.

Claims 1 and 10 have been amended for clarification. Claims 1 and 10 further recite the structure of the shaft having a first end and a second end. The shaft has a first and second end that are different - different dimensions and orientation. That is, the first and second ends have distinct structures which allow the respective ends to move differently in the first and second sockets as claimed. That is, the first end and first socket have a structure that allows for the segment to move in a roll axis where the second socket allows for movement along a pitch axis. That is, the segment facilities roll and pitch movement.

Smith et al. does not teach each and every element of the claimed subject or the elements arranged as recited. In contrast, Smith et al. utilizes a structure where the shaft 4 is a cylinder with a flared end 4a. However, this shaft 4 is not the same in structure as the claimed shaft and further then cannot be considered to function the same when provided in the first and second cavities.

With respect to claim 1, Smith et al. does not disclose "a shaft having a first end and a second end, wherein the first end and the second end have different dimensions and wherein the second end is positioned transverse to an axis of the shaft" or "the first socket is engageable with the first end of the shaft to facilitate movement in a roll axis, and the second socket is engageable with the second end of the shaft to facilitate movement along a pitch axis."

With respect to claim 10, Smith et al. does not disclose "a shaft having a first end and a second end wherein the first end comprises a sphere and the second end comprises a cylinder offset in orientation from an axis of a length of the shaft;" nor "the first socket is engageable with the first end of the shaft to facilitate movement in a roll axis, and the second socket is engageable with the second end of the shaft to facilitate movement along a pitch axis."

At least in view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that Smith does not meet or make obvious the claimed subject matter. It is respectfully requested this rejection be withdrawn and the claims allowed.

Claims 1 and 5-13 are rejected under 35 USC 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Hida (US 4,109,398). Applicant respectfully disagrees with this contention. However, the claims have been amended for clarification.

Claims 1 and 10 have been amended for clarification. Claims 1 and 10 further recite the structure of the shaft having a first end and a second end. The shaft has a first and second end that are different - different dimensions and orientation. That is, the first and second ends have distinct structures which allow the respective ends to move differently in the first and second sockets as claimed. That is, the first end and first socket have a structure that allows for the segment to move in a roll axis where the second socket allows for movement along a pitch axis. That is, the segment facilities roll and pitch movement.

Hida does not teach each and every element of the claimed subject or the elements arranged as recited. In contrast, Hida utilizes a structure where the metal shaft 42 has couplings 44 and 45 secured to its respective ends and a ring gear 43 is disposed between them, also fixed to the shaft. However, this shaft 42 is not the same in structure as the claimed shaft and further then cannot be considered to function the same when provided in the first and second cavities.

With respect to claim 1, Hida does not disclose "a shaft having a first end and a second end, wherein the first end and the second end have different dimensions and wherein the second end is positioned transverse to an axis of the shaft" or "the first socket is engageable with the first end of the shaft to facilitate movement in a roll axis, and the second socket is engageable with the second end of the shaft to facilitate movement along a pitch axis."

With respect to claim 10, Hida does not disclose "a shaft having a first end and a second end wherein the first end comprises a sphere and the second end comprises a cylinder offset in orientation from an axis of a length of the shaft;" nor "the first socket is engageable with the first end of the shaft to facilitate movement in a roll axis, and the second socket is engageable with the second end of the shaft to facilitate movement along a pitch axis."

At least in view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that Smith does not meet or make obvious the claimed subject matter. It is respectfully requested this rejection be withdrawn and the claims allowed.
III. Claim Rejections - 35 USC Q 103

Claims 11-13 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Smith et al. (US 4,283,152). Applicant respectfully disagrees with this contention and for at least the reasons stated above with respect to claim 10 as distinguished from the disclosure of Smith et al. Applicant asserts that the amended claims are neither taught nor suggested by the cited references. Therefore, Application respectfully requests removal of this rejection under § 103.

It is respectfully submitted that the claims are neither met nor made obvious by the cited prior art. At least in view of the above, it is respectfully requested the rejections be withdrawn and all of the claims allowed.
The Director is authorized to charge any fee deficiency required by this paper or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 23-1123.
